answer: WITH p AS (SELECT s.stellarref, s.hostplname, o.period, LAG(o.period) OVER (PARTITION BY s.stellarref ORDER BY o.period) AS prev, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.stellarref ORDER BY o.period) AS rn FROM stars s JOIN planets pl ON pl.hostlink = s.stellarref JOIN orbital_characteristics o ON o.bodylink = pl.planetref WHERE s.compcount > 1 AND o.period > 0), g AS (SELECT stellarref, hostplname, MIN(period) FILTER (WHERE rn = 1) AS inner_p, MAX(period/prev) AS maxr, EXP(AVG(LN(period/prev))) AS gm, COUNT(prev) AS npairs FROM p GROUP BY stellarref, hostplname) SELECT hostplname, ROUND(gm::numeric, 3) AS geometric_mean_period_ratio FROM g WHERE npairs > 0 AND maxr < 3 AND inner_p < 10 ORDER BY gm DESC

WITH o AS (SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.stellarref) s.stellarref, s.hostplname, (s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Mass_Value')::float AS recorded_mass, POWER(oc.semimajor,3)/POWER(oc.period/365.25,2) AS calculated_mass FROM stars s JOIN planets p ON p.hostlink = s.stellarref JOIN orbital_characteristics oc ON oc.bodylink = p.planetref WHERE s.compcount > 1 AND oc.semimajor IS NOT NULL AND oc.period > 0 ORDER BY s.stellarref, oc.semimajor DESC) SELECT hostplname, recorded_mass, calculated_mass FROM o ORDER BY ABS(recorded_mass - calculated_mass) NULLS LAST
note: Period converted days->years with 365.25; outermost chosen among planets with known positive period.

answer: SELECT s.hostplname || ' ' || p.completter AS planet_full_name, s.hostplname AS host_star, o.eccentricity, ROUND((pp.massjup * 1.898E27 / ((s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Mass_Value')::float * 1.98847E30))::numeric, 5) AS mass_ratio FROM planets p JOIN stars s ON s.stellarref = p.hostlink JOIN orbital_characteristics o ON o.bodylink = p.planetref JOIN physical_properties pp ON pp.objectlink = p.planetref JOIN data_quality_tracking d ON d.targetlink = p.planetref WHERE o.eccentricity > 0.25 AND LOWER(d.masssource) LIKE '%msini%' AND pp.massjup IS NOT NULL AND (s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Mass_Value')::float > 0 ORDER BY pp.massjup * 1.898E27 / ((s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Mass_Value')::float * 1.98847E30) ASC

WITH pl AS (SELECT p.hostlink, pp.massjup, pp.densvalue FROM planets p JOIN physical_properties pp ON pp.objectlink = p.planetref WHERE pp.densvalue IS NOT NULL OR pp.massjup IS NOT NULL), h AS (SELECT hostlink FROM pl GROUP BY hostlink HAVING bool_or(densvalue > 3) AND NOT bool_or(COALESCE(massjup > 0.1, false))) SELECT ROUND(AVG(POWER((s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Radius_Value')::float,2) * POWER((s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Temp_Value')::float/5778,4))::numeric, 4) AS avg_luminosity FROM stars s JOIN h ON h.hostlink = s.stellarref WHERE (s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Radius_Value')::float IS NOT NULL AND (s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Temp_Value')::float IS NOT NULL

SELECT ROUND(AVG((s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Temp_Value')::float * SQRT((s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Radius_Value')::float*6.957E8/(2*o.semimajor*1.496E11)))::numeric, 0) AS avg_equilibrium_temperature_k FROM planets p JOIN stars s ON s.stellarref = p.hostlink JOIN physical_properties pp ON pp.objectlink = p.planetref JOIN orbital_characteristics o ON o.bodylink = p.planetref WHERE pp.massjup > 0.1 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM planet_instrument_observations pio JOIN instruments_surveys i ON i.instrumentref = pio.facilitylink WHERE pio.subjectlink = p.planetref AND LOWER(i.facilityname) = 'k2') AND (s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Temp_Value')::float > 0 AND (s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Radius_Value')::float > 0 AND o.semimajor > 0

SELECT (s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Temp_Value')::float AS effective_temperature, ROUND((POWER((s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Radius_Value')::float,2) * POWER((s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Temp_Value')::float/5778,4))::numeric, 3) AS luminosity FROM stars s WHERE LOWER(s.hostplname) = '55 cnc'

SELECT p.completter, s.hostplname, ROUND(((s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Temp_Value')::float * SQRT((s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Radius_Value')::float*6.957E8/(2*o.semimajor*1.496E11)))::numeric, 0) AS equilibrium_temperature_k FROM planets p JOIN stars s ON s.stellarref = p.hostlink JOIN orbital_characteristics o ON o.bodylink = p.planetref LEFT JOIN physical_properties pp ON pp.objectlink = p.planetref WHERE NOT COALESCE(pp.massjup > 0.1 AND o.period < 10, false) AND (s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Temp_Value')::float > 0 AND (s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Radius_Value')::float > 0 AND o.semimajor > 0 ORDER BY (s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Temp_Value')::float * SQRT((s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Radius_Value')::float*6.957E8/(2*o.semimajor*1.496E11)) DESC LIMIT 1

SELECT s.hostplname, o.period, o.inclination, SQRT(6.674E-11 * (s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Mass_Value')::float * 1.989E30 / (o.semimajor * 1.496E11)) / 1000 AS orbital_velocity_km_s FROM planets p JOIN stars s ON s.stellarref = p.hostlink JOIN orbital_characteristics o ON o.bodylink = p.planetref JOIN physical_properties pp ON pp.objectlink = p.planetref WHERE pp.massjup > 0.1 AND o.period < 10 AND o.inclination > 90 AND (s.stellarprops->'physical'->>'Mass_Value')::float IS NOT NULL AND o.semimajor IS NOT NULL ORDER BY orbital_velocity_km_s DESC
note: Returns 0 rows on this data: no planet with inclination > 90 is a hot jupiter. G=6.674e-11, Msun=1.989e30, AU=1.496e11 assumed.

answer: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.stellardist * 3.26156)::numeric, 2) AS avg_distance_ly FROM stars s WHERE s.stellarref IN (SELECT p.hostlink FROM planets p JOIN physical_properties pp ON pp.objectlink = p.planetref JOIN data_quality_tracking d ON d.targetlink = p.planetref WHERE pp.massjup > 0.1 AND pp.densvalue < 0.5 AND (d.limitflags->'stellar_limits'->>'Dist_Lim')::int = 0) AND (s.stellarprops->'photometry'->>'Mag_Blend')::int = 0
note: Null Mag_Blend treated as not-cleared (strict = 0); treating null as not blended would give a different average.

answer: SELECT ROUND(AVG((pp.massjup * 317.83) / POWER(pp.radjup * 11.209, 2))::numeric, 2) AS avg_surface_gravity FROM planets p JOIN physical_properties pp ON pp.objectlink = p.planetref WHERE pp.massjup * 317.83 > 1 AND pp.massjup * 317.83 <= 10 AND pp.densvalue > 3 AND pp.radjup > 0 AND LOWER(p.discmethod) IN ('transit','tr','transit method','photometry','photometric')
note: 'Larger than Earth' read as mass > 1 Earth mass.
